Wave Properties: A wave is a disturbance that transfers energy without carrying matter along. Its crest is the highest point and the trough the lowest. The wavelength (lambda) is the distance between two neighboring crests, the amplitude is the maximum displacement from rest, and the frequency (f) is the number of waves per second in hertz. The period is T = 1 / f. The speed of a wave is v = f x lambda. In a transverse wave the medium moves at right angles to the direction of the wave; in a longitudinal wave it moves back and forth along it. A wave's speed depends on the medium, not on its frequency or amplitude.
Sound Waves: Sound is a longitudinal wave made of compressions and rarefactions that needs a medium; it cannot travel through a vacuum. Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases. In air at room temperature its speed is about 343 m/s. Pitch depends on frequency: a higher frequency is a higher pitch. Loudness depends on amplitude and is measured in decibels. Reflection of sound produces an echo. For an echo, the sound travels to the wall and back, so the distance to the wall is half the total path.
Reflection and Refraction: When a wave hits a surface it can be reflected. The law of reflection says that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal, a line at right angles to the surface. When light passes from one material to another it can change speed and bend; this is refraction. Going from air into a denser material such as water or glass, light bends toward the normal; going back into air it bends away from the normal. A plane mirror forms an upright image of the same size that appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
The Electromagnetic Spectrum: Electromagnetic waves are transverse waves of electric and magnetic fields that can travel through a vacuum at the speed of light, about 3 x 10^8 m/s. In order of increasing frequency (and decreasing wavelength) the spectrum is radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays. All obey v = f x lambda with v = c. Radio waves carry broadcasts, microwaves heat food and carry phone signals, infrared is felt as heat, ultraviolet causes sunburn, X-rays image bones and gamma rays come from nuclear processes. Higher frequency waves carry more energy.
Light, Color and Lenses: White light is a mixture of all colors. A prism splits it into a spectrum because different colors refract by different amounts. The color of an opaque object is the color it reflects; the other colors are absorbed. A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges (brings together) light rays; a concave lens is thinner in the middle and spreads rays apart. A concave mirror curves inward and can focus light, while a convex mirror curves outward and always forms a smaller, upright image of a distant object.
